newsitem.title: UK: Elf eyes chemicals acquisitions -- report.
newsitem.headline: Elf eyes chemicals acquisitions -- report.

text.p: France's Elf Aquitaine was looking to buy speciality chemicals businesses to increase its strength in Asia and the United States, the Financial Times reported on Monday. Although most deals were likely to be relatively small, chairman Philippe Jaffre said a purchase worth 10-15 billion French francs ($1.85-$2.77 billion) would not be out of range, the paper reported. "We now have the capacity to take on enough debt for a real project," he was quoted as saying.
Elf's debt was about 30 billion francs, supported by shareholders' funds of 80 billion francs, the paper said.
The company was likely to seek acquisitions in acrylics in North America, and flourine chemicals, sulphur-based chemicals and adhesives in Asia, the report said.

Jaffre also said he was prepared for the company's stake in its pharmaceuticals unit, Elf Sanofi, to sink to between 20 and 40 percent as part of a previously-announced plan to merge the unit with another drugs group, the paper said. Elf currently held about 53 percent of Sanofi. ($1=5.409 French Franc)
